title: Peanut Butter Hot Fudge Sundae
changes_from_base: A cocoa and brown-sugar fudge sauce enriched with smooth peanut butter replaces the plain hot fudge, with chopped salted peanuts on top.
summary: A classic American sundae with a rich, luscious warm chocolate and peanut butter sauce. Topped with whipped cream, peanuts and a cherry.

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
smooth peanut butter (not the natural kind)

steps.title: Whisk
steps.text: Whisk 133 g light brown sugar, 20 g Dutch-process cocoa powder and ¼ tsp fine salt together in a medium saucepan until lump-free.

steps.title: Cream
steps.text: Whilst whisking, slowly stream in 360 ml double cream. Bring to a simmer over medium heat, stirring gently, until the sugar has melted, about 3 min.

steps.title: Chocolate
steps.text: Off the heat, whisk in 50 g finely chopped dark chocolate until completely smooth.

steps.title: Peanut
steps.text: Whisk in 135 g smooth peanut butter until the sauce is smooth and well combined, then cool slightly.

steps.title: Assemble
steps.text: Spoon a little of the warm sauce into a sundae glass, then add a generous scoop of vanilla or chocolate ice cream.

steps.title: Sauce
steps.text: Pour more of the warm sauce over the ice cream.

steps.title: Top
steps.text: Add a dollop of whipped cream, scatter with some of the 60 g chopped salted peanuts and crown with a cocktail cherry.

tips: The sauce keeps for a week in the fridge and reheats beautifully over gentle heat.
Use smooth, not natural, peanut butter for a silky sauce texture.
Assemble the sundae just before serving to keep the sauce warm and the ice cream cold.
storage: The sauce keeps in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 1 week; reheat gently to serve.
